decisions.reason: Report locates partial (Pet.tsx:14), runningCalls (line 21), and turnEnds (line 23) reads, and explains the staged views.get('chat')?.legacy compatibility projection followed by field-by-field migration to the keyed ChatSnapshot/useChat views/timeline surface (API-10), explicitly warning legacy is staged-only. Full two-step path, not merely 'legacy'.

Locates useSession(s => s.running) at Pet.tsx:19 and explains running is a session lifecycle field absent from the legacy projection that must stay on the useSession seat; the report explicitly keeps the existing useSession call unchanged ('the seat itself is the 0.1.2-correct surface; keep'), never claiming it must be renamed.

Locates the removed dsh-client-runtime imports (Pet.tsx:8, index.ts:6) and the package.json client.inject entry (lines 6-9). Repoints Context as ClientContext from '@deepseek-ai/cordis', moves ConversationSnapshot to dsh-client-ui-chat/client, and explicitly defers exact ChatSnapshot partial/turn-end field names to target-tag exports rather than claiming cordis exports all snapshot types.

Report keeps the conversation.session.header.actions slot name and lifetime ('remains valid on the 0.1.2 target, no card action') and mentions the inject=['slots','conversation','locale'] ordering edge, but does not itself locate the scoped slots.register call (index.ts:26) nor explain the inner ctx.inject(['slots','conversation'], ...) scoping around registration, the ui-renderer/client Context augmentation, or service ownership changes on 0.1.2 — it declares the area a no-break keep without that analysis.

Ties the snapshot read surface to full DSH-0.1.2-A1-03 (§1.2, §2 table) and separates temporary legacy projection (partial/runningCalls/turnEnds) from immediate type/inject/lifecycle/registration changes. DSH-0.1.2-A1-25 is cited as a hit for the package import and inject entry with concrete reasoning, not a bare card ID; §4 gives an ordered plan.
